# Pending changes (since patch 0028, 2026-11-27)

## 2026-11-27 - Mountains, valleys and canyons; climbing

Asked: "introduce mountains, valleys and canyons in planet terrains", then "add the ability to climb mountains,
buildings and tall assets" (and: planets may grow if the terrain needs it - not needed: the continents and chains
are drawn on the unit sphere, a bigger world has the same share of rough ground; sizing stays tied to the orbits).

**Terrain** (PlanetShape.raw_height; TERRAIN per type [mountains, valleys, canyons]: ocean 1/1/0.45, ice 0.9/1.2/0.4,
volcanic 1.2/0.5/1, moon 0.55/0.35/0.8; mountains also x0.75-1.25 by the look's ridges):
- Mountain chains: long belts along the zero lines of a new low-frequency noise (_belt, 2 octaves), inland (from the
  continents' middles - the coasts left low for the towns), ridged peaks on a broad rise: up to ~3 amp more
  (ocean world of 3040 m: peaks ~300 m, was ~150).
- Valleys: a branching network (|noise| near 0, metres: 1/1500 m, ~150 m wide), U-shaped, cut shallow in the
  lowlands (amp x 0.05) and deep in the heights (72% of the height over amp x 0.15); on sea worlds dry (floor >= 4 m).
- Canyons: narrow (~25-35 m half-width), winding (domain warp), three ledges down steep walls, flat floors, in the
  basins far from the chains (|belt noise| > 0.3); their floors down to amp x 0.06 under the sea level on sea
  worlds: rivers (water / ice / lava).
- top() covers the chains (atmosphere, clouds, bounds follow). The target view's "relief" shows top().
- Terrain shader: strata on steep rock (layers by height, wavering).
- Cost: 2.27 -> 2.51 us a height sample (+10%).
- Towns: sites on level highland too (h0 up to amp x 1.5 instead of 0.6), the ring's levelness 22 m (was 14 -
  the town's ground is levelled anyway, blended over 60 m), 400 tries (was 120: rugged worlds). Home system: Amnissos
  5 towns, Ida 3 (8 sample ocean worlds: 13 towns, was 14).
- floor_below (dug ground): looked for from the ground's face down when high above it (it searched 24 m under the
  feet in the air - the jet pack's height read 23 m at 1.6 km over a dug pit).

**Climbing** (CosmosWalker):
- Steep ground (rise > STEEP 1.1 a metre, ~48 deg): climbed as you go, up or down, facing it, CLIMB 1.2 m/s
  vertical; kept on the ground going down (no falling off a cliff's face); 0.4-1.1 rise: slower uphill (to 55%).
- Walls: press into one and Space takes hold (Cosmos.walker_bumps -> note_wall: only what's solid to climb - a town's
  buildings, builds, deposits, dug walls, tall boulders - not people or the ship's legs). W/S up/down (towards/away),
  A/D along, Space jumps off; a ledge ahead within a step of the feet pulls you up onto it (roofs); the wall's face
  kept while climbing. No gravity or jet pack while holding on. Walking into a wall still stops you.
- Tall boulders' tops are floors (_rock_top: a dome over 85% of their radius) - stood on once climbed.
- New clip "climb" (moves.py climb(), CLIMB_STRIDE 1.2 m a 1 s cycle, the holds still on the face; played backwards
  going down, still when holding on). Player model re-exported (art/player_3d, the user's overrides merged as usual).

Tests: test_cosmos.test_climbing_cliffs (new), test_towns_palaces_and_people (climbs the wing's wall onto its roof),
test_land_on_any_world (mountain flanks: flown off to land - rings out to 300 m). Docs: game.md (the land,
climbing; controls).

## 2026-11-27 - Underwater canyons, abysses, caves in the ground

Asked: "make also canyons as well underwater and abyss points with caves, caves no longer make their own instance
they are continuous gameplay and terrain".

- **Seabed canyons**: the canyons also cut the sea worlds' floors (where the continent noise is under the sea,
  in the basins between the chains): trenches their full depth (no river clamp under the sea).
- **Abysses** (sea worlds, ABYSSES 3): sinkholes in the deep sea floor (55-85 m wide), four ledges down to
  amp x 1.8-2.3 under the sea level (~110-190 m), a low lip round them - in the heightfield itself (every LOD,
  cheap: a dot product each); PlanetShape._ab_*.
- **Caves are the ground's own now** (were an instance far off - CosmosDungeon, kind "cave"; dungeons keep theirs):
  PlanetShape.caves - LAND_CAVES 3 into hillsides (a slope of 0.3-1.2, level for 10 m then down to ~28 m deep,
  wandering, kept above the sea on sea worlds) and one into each abyss's wall (flooded: swum). Each a winding
  passage of carves (r 2.4-3.4 m every half radius) with up to 3 branches, a chamber at each end (r 5-7.5 m, a few
  overlapping carves), the deepest a hall (x1.6). 485-1157 carves a world. Drawn by the voxels (CosmosVoxels),
  walked by the floor_below / walls / ceilings of the digging.
  - Made on a worker (make_caves: reads only the noises) and carved in on the main thread (merge_caves: 2-6 ms,
    one world a frame); CosmosPlanet.caves_ready (settled() waits for it). Not saved (from the seed); the save's
    digs are only yours (dig_n - cave_n; DIG_MAX counts yours).
  - The carves' lookups: digs_near from the hash's cells (was a scan of every carve - thousands now); a flag per
    carve "opens the ground" (its 6th float): the patches (plants, boulders) and the terrain shader's cuts take
    only those; the voxels all. Chunks deep under the ground drawn within 90 m (DEEP_SEEN).
  - Cosmos: dungeons_of lists 2 dungeons + the caves (names; ABYSS_NAMES); a hillside cave's arch of boulders round
    its real opening; no "Enter" for a cave. _cave_life: within CAVE_NEAR 150 m of its mouth or a chamber its dead
    wake (1-2 a chamber - skeletons, demons in the deepest - and the demon lord), a bronze chest (lid, a warm glow
    while shut) on the deepest chamber's floor; "Open the chest" (once: "looted" as before); gone past 300 m.
  - CosmosNpc.cave_foe / _cave_fight: a cave's dead walk the carved floor, kept out of its walls, come for you
    about their level; out of sight (40 m), still.
  - The walker under the ground: the rock overhead holds you down (a jump, the jet pack, swimming up).
  - The camera in dug ground: the heightfield's samples skipped where it's carved (it was pressed to your back in
    any tunnel under a hill - player-dug ones too).
- Tests: test_caves_in_the_ground (walked in under the hill, the dead, the lord walks the floor and fights, the
  chest, the ceiling, put away far off), test_abysses_under_the_sea (depths, a cave each, trenches),
  test_caves_and_dungeons (2 dungeons + caves), digging (the save holds yours).
- Frame rate: on foot ~5-9% lower with the caves near (472 vs 517 fps); the same scenes on the last patch on this
  machine today: 457 / 365 fps (mine 472 / 344) - the baseline (694) is from a quieter day. Loading from the title:
  worst frame 50 ms (the last patch: 72 ms on the same run - its drawing).
- Docs: game.md (Caves; Dungeons; the land: trenches, abysses); the cave shot retaken in a real cave (shots.json:
  caption, sources, notes).

## 2026-11-27 - Dungeons in the ground, sliding, a climb and a slide clip, fixes

there is something happening to the collision and suddenly it turns me towards the mountain instead of away from it,

- **Sliding** (the bug: going down a steep slope climbed down it backwards, turned to face the mountain): down ground
  too steep to walk you now slide on your feet, facing down it, up to SLIDE 7.5 m/s along the slope (less across
  the ground the steeper it is), steered across it a little; kept on it at speed (the stick reach grows with speed
  and steepness - a 73-degree slope lost you at 0.8 m). Up it, still a climb. New clip "slide" (moves.py: crouched,
  leaning back, feet staggered down the slope, arms out); the "climb" clip (made last round) shown in the guide.
- **Dungeons in the ground** (were an instance 40 km off, entered by E): PlanetShape.dungeons (made with the caves on
  the worker; the planet's towns known first - kept clear): under a gateway on level ground, sunk so the ground
  over all of it is DUNGEON_ROCK 4 m thick at least (sampled 6x6 over it), above the sea on sea worlds (else no
  dungeon there: the sea's face would cut its rooms); its rooms, corridors and doorway carved as boxes
  (CosmosDungeon.boxes_of - the carves' density takes boxes now, straight-walled; carved_near knows them); a passage
  of carves from the gateway down at 30 degrees, the last 6 m level, through a new west doorway of its first room
  (the fake stairs gone). CosmosDungeon.layout shared by its mesh and its carving; the node a child of its planet,
  built within 260 m (DUNGEON_NEAR), its dead woken when built, put away past 440 m. Cosmos.dungeon = the one you're
  in: no sun, no markers, the surface (patches, sea, sky shells, towns, star) not drawn and not refined, the carved
  rock only by its doorway; your lamp off (its torches, the indoor light). Its floors / walls / roof stand for the
  rock while you're in it (floor_at, walker_bumps, camera) - none of the density's sums. The dead fight only on
  their level. Chest: "Open the chest" by it; no "Enter" / "Climb out".
- **Bolts underground** hit the carved rock, not the ground's face far above (every shot in a cave or a dungeon burst
  at the muzzle - smoke filling the screen: dungeon scene 307 -> 380 fps by that alone).
- floor_at under dry land: no sea clamp (a dungeon's floor below the sea's level floated you at it).
- The jet pack's plumes: a rebuilt pack's freed plumes skipped (the "previously freed instance" error on gate jumps).
- Frame rate: in a dungeon 444 fps (the old instanced one 617 on the same day: a different view; GPU-bound 1.9 ms);

## 2026-11-28 - A detailed dragonfly

Asked: "dragonfly creature is too simplistic make a more detailed and sophisticated model". The dragonfly was the
generic flyer (a ball body, two flat ellipsoid wings, a cone tail); now its own procedural model (CosmosDragonfly) -
a true Anisoptera at the species' unchanged size: a head that's mostly a wrap-around compound-eye dome (hexagonal
facets in the shader, a dark pseudopupil that follows you, the seam where the eyes meet on top), a face, mouthparts,
short antennae; a robust slanted thorax with pale side stripes; six thin jointed legs (spined tibiae, claws) folded
forward under it in flight; a long abdomen of ten tapering segments (dark joints, pale spots along the top, claspers
at the tip); four long narrow wings, the hind pair broader at the base - glass-clear with a faint rainbow sheen,
their veins, cross-veins, trailing-edge cells, nodus, dark stigma and amber base all in the shader. The body
metallic and iridescent (the species' two colours shifting with the angle, a thin-film rainbow over them). The wings
beat in the vertex shader (stroke, twist, a lagging tip; the hind pair a quarter beat ahead; 13 Hz hovering, 18 Hz
darting); it hovers with tiny bobs, darts at four times its pace, pitches into its accelerations, rolls into turns,
flexes its abdomen a little. ~3,000 + 930 vertices, built once on a worker (~6 ms), shared; 2 draw calls a
dragonfly (8 mesh instances before). The other species unchanged. Files: scripts/world/life/cosmos_dragonfly.gd
(new), shaders/world/dragonfly.gdshader + dragonfly_wing.gdshader (new), scripts/world/life/cosmos_creature.gd,
scripts/world/life/cosmos_fauna.gd, scripts/world/models/cosmos_warm.gd (both shaders warmed at the title),
tests/test_dragonfly.gd (new).

## 2026-11-28 - The aeromanta, a sky manta

Asked: "improve also the aeromanta model and animation". The aeromanta was the generic flyer (a ball body, two flat
ellipsoid wings flapping on hinges, a cone tail); now its own procedural model (CosmosAeromanta) at the species'
unchanged size: a broad diamond disc that is its wings - built across its span as 49 rounded wing sections, thick
and domed over the body, thinning to falcate tips, curved swept-back leading edges, a concave trailing edge, a
squared-off wide mouth - scrolled cephalic fins forward of it, glassy eyes on the sides of the head, pelvic fins, a
small dorsal fin and a long thin whip tail; a photoreal skin (a dark mottled back in its first colour with pale
chevron shoulder marks, a pale belly with dark spots and darker edges, five gill slits a side and a dark mouth
underneath, a faint wet sheen). It swims the air: waves travelling from the body out to the wingtips (the vertex
shader, the lighting bent along), in bouts of strokes and long glides (faster fleeing), never still, rising a little
with each stroke, banking into turns, its rippling tail trailing to the outside of them. One shared mesh of 2,315
vertices (a worker, ~6 ms), one draw call an aeromanta (~8 mesh instances before). The frost ray, the ember swarm
queen and the others unchanged. Files: scripts/world/life/cosmos_aeromanta.gd (new), shaders/world/aeromanta.gdshader
(new), scripts/world/life/cosmos_creature.gd, cosmos_fauna.gd, scripts/world/models/cosmos_warm.gd,
tests/test_aeromanta.gd (new), tests/test_dragonfly.gd.

## 2026-11-28 - A realistic red fox

Asked: "red fox model should be much more realistic and detailed with better animations". The fox was the generic
canine (scaled spheres and capsules, legs swinging on pivots); now its own model and rig (CosmosFox), its size,
speeds and temper kept: one procedural skinned mesh (~1,970 vertices) on a 26-bone skeleton - a lean body (deep
chest, tucked waist), a thick neck with a white throat, a narrow skull with white cheek ruffs, the long pointed muzzle
(white chin, a glossy black nose, whiskers), amber eyes with slit pupils, big upright ears with black backs, slender
jointed legs in black stockings over small paws, the bushy white-tipped brush. Its coat (fox.gdshader): soft wrapped
light, fur strands along each part, darker guard hairs, a rim of light, a little light through it. Its gaits chosen
and blended by speed - a 4-beat walk, the trot on diagonal pairs (its own), a rotary gallop (the spine rocking and
flexing) fleeing; its tail hanging and swaying at rest, streaming out running; ears flicking, laid back fleeing;
standing about it looks round, sniffs the ground, sits, and now and then makes its high mousing pounce (a crouch, an
arcing leap, a nose-first dive). Built once on a worker (~5 ms), shared; one draw call a fox (~13 mesh instances
before). The wolves and other canines unchanged. Files: scripts/world/life/cosmos_fox.gd (new), shaders/world/
fox.gdshader (new), scripts/world/life/cosmos_creature.gd, cosmos_fauna.gd, scripts/world/models/cosmos_warm.gd,
tests/test_fox.gd (new).

## 2026-11-28 - Weather, clouds in layers, sun rays, compass and maps

Asked (in turns): "make multiple layers of clouds, some moving faster some slower, different shapes and sizes, also
different weather, rain, storm, snow etc ... particle effects ... different clouds for them. When snowing the snow
accumulates on ground, rain makes the ground wet and muddy ... icons displaying the weather state, temperature and
radioactivity"; "change cloud density depending on the weather, weather is local and not global ... moves across the
planet"; "make sure rain and snow are realistic"; "use sun rays effect for the clouds and seeing the sun through trees";
"the ground should occlude markers" (logged above); "dont let them overlap with the compass"; "on planets the compass
displays longitude and latitude as well, planet map does the same too"; "in space ... no north, south ..."; "compass
should show in space pitch and yaw"; "use a more detailed and better texture for the ground ... greek terrain".
- **PlanetWeather** (new): a world's weather as cells - 5-7 a world with air (ocean 7, ice 6, volcanic 5; none on an
  airless moon), each over its own part (reach 0.28-0.42 of the radius), drifting round on its own great circle at
  0.8-2.2 m/s, living a 700-1300 s cycle (building, raining, dying away), a share of them storms; a pure function of
  the seed and Galaxy.time (the same weather for anyone, after a save). What falls by the temperature (rain, snow
  under 0.5 C, ash on the volcanic worlds); the ground wet / snow lying from each cell, lingering after it (the
  cycle's tail). at(): cover, precip, storm, wet, snow, state (clear, cloudy, rain, storm, snow, blizzard, ash, ash
  storm), temperature (latitude, height, the sun, the weather; airless: blazing in the sun, bitter out of it),
  radioactivity (µSv/h: ocean 0.12, ice 0.18, volcanic 0.65, an airless moon ~30 - more high up, in the sun).
- **Clouds in three layers** (CosmosPlanet.CLOUD_LAYERS): low and heavy (the weather's own - thick and dark under a
  cell, black under a storm; one overcast sheet, no gaps, under strong weather), heaped in the middle, thin streaks
  racing high (stretched noise, x2.6 speed); each its height, scale, drift, shape, softness, opacity; their order
  for the eye (under them the low drawn last). Every world with air has them (weather brings clouds where it's clear).
- **CosmosWeatherFx** (new): the cells to every world's clouds and ground (1.5 s); where you are (4 a second): rain
  (crossed streaks along their fall, 11,000 in 52 m round you, slanting in a storm's wind, splashes flicking up round
  your feet), snow (22,000 flakes of mixed sizes tumbling in the air all round you - not just overhead), ash (grey
  flakes drifting); a storm's lightning (a jagged bolt with a branch or two from the cloud base, its flash, the
  thunder as late as it struck far); the rain's hiss and the wind (loops, if their sounds are there); nothing falls
  indoors, underground, aboard, docked, under the sea. The light under the weather: the sun dimmed (to 40% overcast,
  less in a storm), the shade grey; the weather's veil (the environment's fog - a grey wall of rain, a blizzard's
  whiteout, an ash storm's murk; the falling flakes themselves not lost in it).
- **The ground under the weather** (terrain.gdshader): wet - darker, damp (not a mirror), mud on the bare flats,
  small puddles in the flat hollows near you (glinting: a highlight in light()); snow lying on all but the steep.
- **The HUD's weather** (under your gauge, clear of the compass bar): its icon (sun or moon, cloud, rain, the bolt,
  snow, ash - vector-drawn), the temperature (a thermometer, blue under 0, warm over 38) and the radioactivity (the
  trefoil; amber over 5, red over 50 µSv/h).
- **The sun's rays** (CosmosGodRays, a CompositorEffect after the transparent pass + shaders/world/god_rays.glsl, a
  compute shader in three passes: the open sky near the sun as a mask at half size, smeared along the lines to the
  sun, added to the frame): shafts through the gaps in the clouds and the trees - by day in a world's air, the sun
  ahead of you; less under cloud, none under a storm; golden low. Not in the browser's renderer.
- **The compass**: on a world, under the heading, your latitude and longitude; in space no compass points - the yaw
  (Y, degrees round the system's plane) and under it the pitch off that plane (P). The planet map: your own latitude
  and longitude in its details (its globe already gridded every 30 degrees).
- **The ground close up, Greek** (terrain.gdshader `greek`: the ocean worlds 1, elsewhere a touch): red terra rossa
  showing through, pale limestone breaking out (mostly where it's steep), stones scattered, dry golden grass on the
  gentle sunny ground - at 3 m and half a metre, fading in near you; its grain in the light (a bump at half a metre).
- Docs: game.md (Weather, The sun's rays, the compass, the planet map) and new shots space3d_storm, space3d_snow,
  space3d_rays (the guide's shots set up the weather by winding the clock to a cell's strongest moment over land).
- Fixes on the way: the shaders' `continue` in the cells loop replaced (a branch-free loop); a QuadMesh's material
  set through its own `material` (not surface_set_material); cloud cover can close to a sheet.

## 2026-11-28 - The automaton: the rifle folds to the hip, jet thrusters in the soles, a shield
Asked: remove the jet pack model; the gun folds into pieces and holsters on the hip (animations to match); the jet
pack becomes jet thrusters coming out of the soles of the feet; the automaton gets a shield like a spaceship's.
- **No jet pack**: the pack's mesh on the back is gone (and its warm-up); the upgrade is "Jet thrusters".
- **The rifle folds**: its stock, barrel and sights on their own bones in the Blender rig (kit.py / automaton.py /
  build.py), folding into a short block that sits in a holster on the right hip; the draw unfolds it on the way to
  the hands, the holster folds it back (moves.py: the draw / holster clips re-keyed; the arms layer's carry poses
  from the hip, arms_layer.gd). art/player_3d re-exported.
- **Jet thrusters**: flames from under each foot (on the foot bones; their length and glow with the burn, a flicker),
  their light under you; the same charge, upgrades and flight as before (cosmos_walker.gd `_thrusters_on`).
- **The shield**: 60 points round the automaton, taking blows before the hull (its health) - a bubble flashing where
  it's hit; back at 15 a second 3 s after the last blow. The gauge's ring round your health shows it, as a ship's.
- **The user's edited character** (a mesh-editor variant over the generated model): ModelOverride now gives it the
  model's current clips (the moves follow the model: climbing, sliding, the new draw and holster), the tracks for
  bones its skeleton hasn't got left out; clips only it has kept. Its own rifle has no fold bones: it hangs at the
  hip whole until the variant is saved again from the new model.
- Tests: the rifle holstered at the hip; the animals' and the dungeons' bites with the shield down first; the
  override test's new rule; the compass test in space (yaw and pitch, no compass points).

## 2026-11-28 - Roads, caravans and loot
Asked: enemies, NPCs and creatures always drop loot; planets have several cities and villages joined by road
systems, with logistics - caravans and other travellers going between them, who may be attacked, looted and die.
- **Loot** (CosmosLoot, new; shaders/world/loot.gdshader): every death leaves a leather pouch (one shared lathed
  mesh, 188 vertices, its bronze clasp glinting) - its contents by what died: animals game meat, raw hides, bones
  (alien ones cybernetic matter, monsters titan bones and void crystals); pirates and raiders drachmas, charges,
  weapon parts, ore; skeletons old coins, relic shards, Linear tablets, amber; demons chimera embers (the lord a
  hoard); travellers their goods or pay. "Loot the ..." in reach (the grabbing hand): taken with the pick-up move,
  into the inventory as far as the hold allows, logged. Pouches last 240 s (a robbed caravan's remains 900 s).
  New items: Game Meat, Raw Hide, Beast Bones (items.gd, with icons).
- **More towns**: worlds get 0-2 more cities and 1-2 more villages (at least 1.7 km apart), appended after the old
  sites - the old towns stay where they were (saves, maps).
- **Roads** (CosmosRoads, new; shaders/world/road.gdshader): a spanning tree of the cheapest ways plus a few
  shortcuts, each by A* over the ground (34 m cells in a band round the great circle; steep ground dear, sea and
  lava shut, ice dear), smoothed and sampled every 3 m - on a worker within 9 km of a world (0.02-1.6 s a world;
  1-8 roads of 1.7-10 km). Drawn as ribbons draped on the ground (1.5 m rows, six across; ~190 m pieces built on
  workers within 1.1 km), packed earth with ruts, a grassy crown, pebbles - cobbles fading into earth in the last
  260 m out of a city. Nothing grows on them (PlanetShape bare zones).
- **Logistics and travellers** (CosmosCaravans, CosmosTraveller, new): each town makes 3 goods and uses up the
  rest; caravans load what their town has most of and the other least, and unload it there. Caravans (guards,
  traders, 1-2 pack donkeys), couriers, pilgrims, patrols - numbers along a road when far, people within 320 m
  (one a frame), back to numbers past 360 m. Pirate-camp raiders ambush them, hunting beasts go for them; guards
  fight back (real bolts), the unarmed run; out of sight a raid is settled by the odds. Shoot at one and its guards
  turn on you. What you witness goes to the event log. Town guards no longer shoot travellers.
- Cost: none measurable on foot. A fix on the way: the indoor lamp no longer reached for a walker that wasn't there.

## 2026-11-28 - Trees and vegetation: Greek flora, real branches and leaves, meadows and woods
Asked: better trees - more variety in design, size and density; far more grass on the green land, several kinds of
grass and low plants; trees and vegetation from Greece only; trees with individual branches and leaves.
- CosmosFlora rewritten. The green (ocean) worlds: olive (gnarled, twisted, several stems, leaves silver beneath)
  and cypress everywhere, a rare dead snag, and 4 of stone pine (an umbrella), Aleppo pine (leaning, sinuous),
  plane (mottled bark, spreading), holm oak, carob, fig, Greek fir (high ground), palm (warm shores); under them
  maquis and phrygana (lentisk mounds, thyme / sage cushions, 2 of broom, oleander, rockrose), 4 grasses (green
  turf, golden dry grass with seed heads, bunch-grass tufts, shore reeds with plumes) and 3 of 5 meadow flowers
  (poppy, daisy, asphodel, anemone, thistle). The other worlds keep their alien flora (crystal, glow and giant
  fungus trees, frosted firs, cacti, fungi).
- A tree is a recursive tapered branch structure - trunk, limbs, branches, twigs - in three detail levels: near
  (within 32 m) twigs carrying leaf cards that the new leaf_flora.gdshader cuts into single leaves (narrow pairs,
  ovals, five-lobed, needle tufts, cypress fronds; each its own shade; leaf-shaped shadows); middle, clump crowns
  fringed with leaf cards; far, coarse clumps. Light through the leaves from behind, their flutter in the wind.
- Sizes from saplings (10%, 0.3-0.6x) to old giants (5%, to 1.45x), most middling; each plant turned, tilted,
  stretched its own way. Placement: a woods noise (~340 m: forests, groves, clearings, lone trees), each species'
  own territory, height bands (shore, lowland, hills, mountains), thinning on slopes, none on beach sand; grass up
  to 80 clumps per 100 m² (~56 blades each), shrinking into the ground by 44 m - meadows thin out, no edge.
- Speed: scattering on the workers, each cell sampled 3x3 first (4.4x faster: 8.8 -> 2.0 ms a finest cell); crowns
  capped at 16 clumps (middle meshes ~1.3-2k triangles); species' meshes one a frame; shadows only on the finest
  patches; the leaf cutting (discard) only in the trees' shader. Patches built before the plants were designed are
  replanted. On foot ~0.7 ms a frame for all of it.
